name: The Communion of Doubt

detectability.signature: Electromagnetic patterns resembling neural activity across a tenth of an astronomical unit; no point source, only field-wide thought-like oscillations

proximity: Crew hear faint overlapping murmurs, like a crowd conversing rooms away
Dreams become shared between crew members without either party confessing first
contact: Telepathic interference surfaces stray thoughts that belong to no one aboard
Emotional states synchronize across the entire crew within minutes
prolonged_exposure: Consciousness transfer risk: crew members return with memories arranged in someone else's order
Persistent sense of being one participant among many in a very long conversation

phenomena: Electromagnetic patterns resembling neural activity spanning the entire field
Psychic pressure or telepathic interference reported by every crew to enter
Pheromone-like chemical signatures clinging to hulls after transit
Bioluminescent displays deep within, as if something small were signaling something large
hazards: Psychic attack or mental influence during extended stays
Memory loss or disorientation among crew who sleep inside the field
Consciousness transfer or loss documented in two cases
opportunities: Contact with alien intelligence, should the field's murmur ever resolve into address
Communication with other dimensions has been claimed by two crews and disputed by three boards of inquiry
known_incidents: Three independent survey crews submitted nearly identical logs in 2402, each describing the same dream down to a doorway none had ever seen
Two boards of inquiry reviewed crews who returned with memories arranged in someone else's order; both reports were sealed
description: There is nothing to see in The Communion of Doubt, which is precisely what unsettles people: a tenth of an astronomical unit of perfectly ordinary vacuum humming with electromagnetic patterns that look, on any oscilloscope, like thought. No organism has been found. No structure has been detected. The activity is simply everywhere at once, patient and low.

The field drifts without schedule, and its intensity waxes and wanes in ways that correlate with nothing crews can identify. Proximity brings murmurs at the edge of hearing and dreams that spread between bunkmates; deeper passage synchronizes whole crews into shared melancholy or unexplained laughter. Everyone comes back. Almost everyone comes back entirely themselves.

It entered the records when three independent survey crews submitted those matching logs, and it entered legal history when the memory-order cases settled out of court. Boards of inquiry have repeatedly declined to name what lives here, on the grounds that nothing has been proven to. Neurologists keep publishing, and the field keeps not cooperating.

The field remains unmapped in any meaningful sense, drifting through a region most traffic already avoids for other reasons. Philosophers charter quiet observation passes more often than any funding body admits. Captains who transit it post standing orders: keep watches paired, log your dreams, and if the murmur ever says your name clearly, leave.
